summary: I includes animals grazing absolutely, grazing vegetation (Hors 2/84; PrS 59/25) and humans tending animals (PrS 10/3, 32/7). III regularly has human herders and animal causees; do not infer the stem from translation alone.
JTM 4.2/16 contrasts marʕenawo af fare with marʕelan laf fare: background Infectum-wa versus completed Preterit, and a possible local patient-marking contrast.
The III Preterit box is newly exemplified by several sources; the inherited III Preterit-wa example actually has Infectum-wa morphology.
roʕənne (78/47) has a likely co-referential l-suffix; the horses remain the grazing subjects, not objects of a causative.
Marʕéwalle at MAC NE Dilo and Falako/24 refers back to turkeys. The category of reduplicated marʕəyone at JTM 1.1/94 cannot be established from this passage alone.
No new lexicalized idiom or light-verb phrase is established.
Finite human herders use III marʕenawo/marʕelən; animals use I roʕən. English graze/herd does not determine the stem.
Jan 2.10/2549 contrasts kmarʕelən with marʕewolən in a single account; the habitual/background form does not constitute a new sense.
The III Infectum-wa cell is already full once the round-1 relocation of 29/283 is applied; claims of only one example are stale.
rʕoyo after kobodən b- securely supplies an activity nominal. The slaughter passage may be allegorical; without broader allowed context no separate figurative human-participant sense is asserted.
Round-1 repair of the split I forms/sense boundary is retained in the human baseline.
Is III marʕele in JTM 1.1/7 used with an animal subject, or is a human keeper implicit?
What is the category of reduplicated marʕəyone at JTM 1.1/94? Does it contain an Infinitiv or Part act. form?
Confirm the antecedent of feminine -o in MAC NI Aḥmad Aġa Oṣman Aġa/46 and object versus unmarked location for pasture in /76.
Is l- in laf fare (JTM 4.2/16) differential patient marking or source phrasing?
At 90/40 the German reads werde, while Koroʕeno means grazing. Check for weide in the edition; no corrected translation is invented.
Check singular roʕe with apparently plural səsye at 70/163.
Does marʕanwole buxatu at Jan 2.4/933 refer to third-plural tenders alongside the addressees?
Is Jan 3.56/1630 an extended allegory? A single grazing nominal does not establish a new lexical sense.
Please provide human translations for publication; the added English is project machine translation.
Poultry and cranes feed/forage, and humans can literally graze like animals. These extend the grazer participant, not the verb meaning.
The expressed pasture in marʕelan i+marʕàṯṯestene and possible pasture-resuming -o in marʕolux may replace the animal theme; their direct-object versus location status remains open.
